KASPER

Back to the slides. Here's the demo again, ring by ring, in William's terms.

Capability, the human: the model read the customer's words, the agent proposed, and a person released the money. A proposal, never an outcome.

Capability, per call: the customer told the model to pay eighty thousand. The model read two thousand four hundred. And when we sent eighty thousand anyway, with the agent's own identity, the gateway said 403. Intent lives in the prompt; capability lives in the gateway. Capability won.

Evidence: every claim read back from the trace. What the customer wrote, what the model read, who decided, which rule, who approved, and AgentEvals' four checks. That's the part we add to the rings: evidence as a byproduct of the checks.

The live level: one flag, and a claim under six thousand settled with no one asked. Only the flag changed.

The keystone: the agent couldn't change that flag, even after RBAC said yes.

And under all of it, the core: every one of those checks keyed off one identity, the settlement agent's SPIFFE ID.

Source: docs/demo-runbook.md §5 "The flow"; William Rizzo, KCD Sofia 2026 (The Safe Operating Model; "When intent and capability disagree, capability wins"; "Evidence is a byproduct")
